messages.subject: Fw: ggplot: plot x position values on graph with y values
parts:
Dave,

here's the sample data:

df<-data.frame(pos=1:4,A=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3),B=c(0.01,0.05,0.1,0.2))
df.melt<-melt(df,id.var=c("pos"))

----- Forwarded by Adam Loveland/FinAdmin/CLE/PNC on 07/20/2012 03:03 PM -----
From: Adam Loveland/FinAdmin/CLE/PNC
To: DavidE <davidroh...@gmail.com>
Cc: ggp...@googlegroups.com
Date: 07/20/2012 03:03 PM
Subject: Re: ggplot: plot x position values on graph with y values



I'd melt the data:

here's one approach. there's probably a less arbitrary way than this when it comes to dodging the pos label from the variable label

#first, melt the data
df.melt <- melt (df,id.var=pos)

#plot same data with two different labels
ggplot(df.melt,aes(pos,variable))+
geom_text(aes(label=variable))+
geom_text(data=subset(df.melt,value>0.1),aes(x=pos+.1,y=variable,label=value))


Adam Loveland


From: DavidE <davidroh...@gmail.com>
To: ggp...@googlegroups.com
Date: 07/20/2012 02:46 PM
Subject: ggplot: plot x position values on graph with y values
Sent by: ggp...@googlegroups.com




ggplot2 users:

A plotting question. I have a data frame consisting of one column of 317 x position values (pos), and 20 columns of y data values (A,C,D,.....), arranged like this:

pos  A    C    D  ...  
1     0.1 0.2 0.01
2     0.4 0.1 0.001
3     0.0 0.05 0.001
.
.
.

I am using ggplot () + geom_text(data=df, aes(pos, A, label="A", colour="red")) to plot out the letter A based on its value. I would also like to plot the pos number next to A if the value of A is >0.1 (to plot A2, for instance). I can manage to do this using the generic plot function using this code:

plot (1:317, df$A[1:10], pch="A", cex=1,col="A")
for (j in 1:nrow(df)) {
       if (df$A[j] >= 0.1) {
           text(j, df$A[j], j,pos=4, offset=0.2,  col="black", cex=0.7)
       }
}

I'm having trouble using the same strategy with ggplot2. I can think of adding additional columns to the data frame to call when plotting - like this:

pos  A    A1  
1     0.1  NA      
2     0.4   2      
3     0.0   NA  
.
.
This solution seems rather clunky. Is there an equivalent strategy for ggplot2?

Thanks for your suggestions.

--

parts:
Adam,

thanks for the suggestion. Seems to be working..

png("ggplot_melt.png", height=300, width=600)
ggplot(df.melt, aes(pos, value)) + geom_text(aes(label=variable,
colour=variable,group=1:6340)) + geom_text(data=subset(df.melt, value > 0.05),aes(x=pos+7,
y=value, size=2,label=pos)) + geom_text(data=subset(df.melt, value < -0.05), aes(x=pos+7,
y=value, size=2, label=pos)) +
opts(legend.position="none",panel.border=theme_rect(size=0.8))
dev.off()




-dave

parts:
On 2012-Jul-20, at 21:56 , DavidE wrote:
>
> thanks for the suggestion. Seems to be working..
>
> png("ggplot_melt.png", height=300, width=600)
> ggplot(df.melt, aes(pos, value)) + geom_text(aes(label=variable,
> colour=variable,group=1:6340)) + geom_text(data=subset(df.melt, value > 0.05),aes(x=pos+7,
> y=value, size=2,label=pos)) + geom_text(data=subset(df.melt, value < -0.05), aes(x=pos+7,
> y=value, size=2, label=pos)) +
> opts(legend.position="none",panel.border=theme_rect(size=0.8))
> dev.off()

If you want to plot several letters as this new example suggest, indeed you need to melt the data

df<-data.frame(pos=1:4,A=c(0,0.1,0.2,0.3), B=c(0.3, 0.2, 0.1, 0))
library("ggplot2")
library("reshape2")
dfm <- melt(df, id.vars="pos")
ggplot(dfm) + geom_text(aes(x=pos, y=value, label=ifelse(value>0.1, paste(variable, value), variable)))
# there a quirk because variable gets transformed into a factor, we want it as character
dfm$variable <- as.character(dfm$variable)
ggplot(dfm) + geom_text(aes(x=pos, y=value, label=ifelse(value>0.1, paste(variable, value), variable)))
